name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that runs after every major design change. It flags low-contrast elements in real time, so designers see violations immediately—not after a user complains or a WCAG audit fails. The trade-off is a small performance hit during rapid prototyping, but it prevents costly fixes later and keeps the interface consistently readable.

name: Pane
text: The live contrast checker risks training designers to ignore warnings like seatbelt chimes—if every minor tweak triggers a red flag, they’ll learn to dismiss them as noise. A better alternative is a pre-commit hook that blocks merges only for severe violations, not every low-contrast pixel, and settles the argument by measuring designer velocity before and after.
